Source library

Wikipedia: Breast Enlargement Methods & Data

Everything the English Wikipedia article “Breast enlargement” covers — definition, methods, extracted facts and references — captured at a fixed revision and linked to the original.

Home/Research library/Wikipedia information

This library captures the content of the English Wikipedia article “Breast enlargement” — its definition, the four methods it lists as actual or potential ways to achieve larger breasts, the one method it lists as ineffective, the facts extracted from the text and all seven of its references. Every entry links back to the original article so the wording and any later edits can be checked at source.

What this library is — and what it is not

Wikipedia is a collaboratively edited, open encyclopedia. It is a starting point for orientation, not medical guidance: its articles are not written or reviewed by a clinician, and its content can change between visits. Nothing here is a recommendation of a method, product or procedure, and individual suitability always requires assessment by a qualified healthcare professional.

The data on this page was captured from revision 1289906330 of the article, last edited on 11 May 2025. Wikipedia articles change over time — always read the current version before relying on any point.

Coverage

What the Wikipedia article covers

A short article with a definition, four methods, one ineffective method, a see-also list and seven references.

Definition and context

Breast enlargement as natural mammoplasia or active intervention, and why breasts matter to self-image, femininity and sexual attractiveness.

Surgical method

Breast augmentation with implants or fat transfer, listed as an actual and potential method and linked to the augmentation articles.

Hormonal method

Pharmacological or hormonal enhancement with medications such as estrogen or breast enlargement supplements, with three supporting citations.

Food energy and KLF14

Increasing food energy intake to add adipose tissue near the breast area, with distribution between individuals controlled by the KLF14 gene.

Mechanical method

Mechanical breast enhancement, cited to a 2007 study of the Brava external tissue expander.

Ineffective methods

The Mark Eden bust developer, named and described as a fraudulently marketed method and device.

The article in brief

Breast enlargement is the enlargement of the breasts. It may occur naturally as in mammoplasia or may occur artificially through active intervention. Many women regard their breasts, which are female secondary sex characteristics, as important to their sexual attractiveness, as a sign of femininity that is important to their sense of self. Due to this, when a woman considers her breasts deficient in some respect, she might choose to engage in some activity intended to enhance them.

Mammoplasia. The article names natural breast enlargement as mammoplasia, distinguishing it from enlargement produced by active intervention.

Methods listed

Methods the article lists to achieve larger breasts

The four actual and potential methods named in the article, with the wording condensed from the source. The right-hand column points to the article’s own references.

Methods the article lists to achieve larger breasts
MethodCategoryWhat the article saysRefs
Surgical breast augmentationSurgicalThe article lists surgical breast augmentation as an actual and potential method to achieve larger breasts, naming two routes: breast implants and fat transfer (fat grafting). It links to the breast augmentation and breast implant articles for the operative detail, cost and risk information held there.—
Pharmacological or hormonal breast enhancementHormonalThe article lists pharmacological or hormonal breast enhancement through administration of medications such as estrogen or breast enlargement supplements. Three of the article's seven citations support this method: two clinical texts on hormone therapy and breast cancer metastasis, and a 1998 study on hormonal breast augmentation and insulin-like growth factor-I (IGF-I).[2] [3] [4]
Increasing food energy intakeWeight and body compositionThe article states that by increasing food energy intake, more adipose tissue will be created, part of which will consist of adipose tissue located near the breast area. The amount added to the breasts varies from person to person and is controlled by the KLF14 gene. The article notes that additional modification of the KLF14 gene can thus make sure even more of the adipose tissue increase will occur at the breasts.[5] [6]
Mechanical breast enhancementMechanical / externalThe article lists mechanical breast enhancement as a potential method, supported by a single citation: a 2007 Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery study evaluating the Brava external tissue expander and asking whether breast enlargement without surgery is a reality.[7]

Statements are condensed from the Wikipedia article “Breast enlargement” (revision 1289906330). Inclusion in the article is not evidence of safety or effectiveness — check the linked references and discuss any option with a qualified clinician.

Ineffective methods

Methods the article lists as ineffective

The article separates methods it describes as actual or potential from those it describes as ineffective.

Methods the article lists as ineffective
MethodCategoryWhat the article saysRefs
Mark Eden bust developerIneffectiveThe article places the Mark Eden bust developer in its list of ineffective methods to achieve larger breasts, describing it as a fraudulently marketed method and device.—

The article names only one ineffective method. Absence of other entries from this list does not mean a method is effective — evidence for each option has to be assessed separately.

Extracted data

Key facts from the article

The statements below condense what the Wikipedia article says about breast enlargement. The right-hand column links to the source article.

Key facts from the article
TopicWhat the article saysSource
DefinitionBreast enlargement is the enlargement of the breasts; it may occur naturally as in mammoplasia or artificially through active intervention.Breast enlargement
Why it is soughtMany women regard their breasts, a female secondary sex characteristic, as important to sexual attractiveness and as a sign of femininity, so a woman who considers her breasts deficient may choose an activity intended to enhance them.Breast enlargement
Surgical methodSurgical breast augmentation — with breast implants or fat transfer — is listed as an actual and potential method to achieve larger breasts.Breast enlargement
Hormonal methodPharmacological or hormonal enhancement through medications such as estrogen or breast enlargement supplements is listed, with citations to a hormone-therapy text, a breast cancer metastasis text and a 1998 study of IGF-I in hormonal breast augmentation.Breast enlargement
Food energy intakeIncreasing food energy intake creates more adipose tissue, part of it located near the breast area; the amount added to the breasts varies between people.Breast enlargement
KLF14 geneThe amount of adipose tissue added to the breasts is controlled by the KLF14 gene, so modification of KLF14 could direct more of the tissue increase to the breasts.Breast enlargement
Mechanical methodMechanical breast enhancement is listed as a potential method, cited to a 2007 study of the Brava external tissue expander.Breast enlargement
Ineffective methodThe Mark Eden bust developer is named as an ineffective method — a fraudulently marketed method and device.Breast enlargement
Article scopeThe article lists four actual or potential methods, one ineffective method and seven references, and is cross-listed in the Wikipedia category 'Breast'.Breast enlargement

Statements are paraphrased from the Wikipedia article. Wikipedia is open content that anyone can edit; verify against the linked article revision before relying on any point.
